back: Every non-clustered index carries the clustered key, so a wide one inflates every index on the table. Keyword: it propagates.
The index found the rows but not all the columns — add them as included columns to cover the query. Keyword: cover it.
Columnstore for analytical scans with high compression; rowstore for point lookups and small ranges. Keyword: scan vs seek.
A SEQUENCE is independent of any table, so several tables can share one series. Keyword: shared series.
In-memory, lock-free structures for high-contention OLTP where latching is the bottleneck. Keyword: contention.
System-versioned history maintained automatically, queried with FOR SYSTEM_TIME. Keyword: what did this look like then.
Temporal records history; ledger proves cryptographically that it was not rewritten. Keyword: record vs prove.
Model nodes and edges natively; MATCH expresses many-hop traversal far more clearly than recursive joins. Keyword: traversal.
Exposes data held elsewhere so it is queried without being copied. Keyword: query in place.
Inline table-valued functions expand into the calling query and optimise with it; scalar functions historically forced row-by-row execution. Keyword: prefer inline.
It extends every transaction touching the table, and chains of triggers are the hardest database logic to debug. Keyword: use sparingly.
They differ in how ties are handled — unique numbering, gaps after ties, or no gaps. Keyword: ties.
Reach adjacent rows, making period-over-period comparison a single pass instead of a self-join. Keyword: one pass.
Shreds a JSON document into rows and columns so it can be queried relationally. Keyword: JSON to table.
EDIT_DISTANCE, EDIT_DISTANCE_SIMILARITY, and JARO_WINKLER_DISTANCE support deduplication and record linkage. Keyword: approximate strings.
Check it before committing — the transaction may be uncommittable and must be rolled back. Keyword: check before commit.
Record project conventions so suggestions match the codebase, versioned with the code so the guidance is reviewable. Keyword: conventions as code.
Connecting an assistant to a database gives it whatever the connection can do — scope the identity, never use a production admin. Keyword: least privilege.

front: TDE does not hide from DBAs
back: It protects files at rest and is transparent to anyone querying. Keyword: not against admins.
Keys live with the client so the engine only sees ciphertext — the only option hiding values from an administrator. Keyword: client-side keys.
Deterministic allows equality comparison but reveals patterns; randomised allows none without an enclave. Keyword: query or hide.
A presentation control for unprivileged users, not a security boundary — the data is unchanged. Keyword: not a boundary.
A predicate function bound to the table, enforced by the engine on every query. Keyword: cannot be bypassed.
Microsoft Entra with a managed identity removes the connection-string secret, usually the weakest link. Keyword: no secret.
Row versioning so readers do not block writers — usually the right change when blocking dominates. Keyword: stop the blocking.
Blocking is waiting; a deadlock is mutual and the engine kills a victim. Keyword: one waits, both stuck.
Identifying a plan regression and forcing the previous plan. Keyword: it was fast last week.
Implies bad cardinality estimates, usually from stale statistics or a parameter-sensitive plan. Keyword: estimates were wrong.
It holds the desired schema; the build produces a DACPAC compared against the target. Keyword: declare the schema.
Comparing the project against a deployed database reports what somebody changed by hand. Keyword: the undocumented change.
So a lookup table is reproducible rather than remembered. Keyword: static data is code.

front: Why deployment gates matter more here
back: A bad schema deployment is far harder to roll back than a bad binary. Keyword: hard to reverse.
Change Tracking records that a row changed and its key, cheaply. CDC records full before and after images, at higher cost. Keyword: key vs images.
Map tables, views, and procedures to REST and GraphQL endpoints with per-role, per-action permissions. Keyword: deliberate exposure.
Relationships produce nested queries — one request returning a graph rather than several REST calls. Keyword: one round trip.

front: Expose a procedure, not the tables
back: Publishing a stored procedure through DAB shares behaviour without exposing the underlying tables. Keyword: behaviour, not schema.
The text a user would actually search against, concatenated where several columns together carry the meaning. Keyword: not identifiers.
Too large dilutes the vector so nothing matches strongly; too small loses context. Overlap preserves severed sentences. Keyword: both directions hurt.
They go stale the moment the source row changes, and nothing errors when they do. Keyword: silent staleness.
Immediate, but adds the model call's latency to every write — usually the wrong trade. Keyword: too expensive inline.
Lets a process pick up changed rows and re-embed out of band — the common answer. Keyword: out of band.
Exact terms, product codes, and names, with stemming and proximity. Keyword: the literal words.
Paraphrases that share no vocabulary, matched by embedding distance. Keyword: meaning.
A product code carries no semantic signal and a paraphrase shares no terms — each method fails where the other succeeds. Keyword: both.
A full-text relevance score and a vector distance are not comparable quantities; rank is meaningful in both lists. Keyword: ranks, not scores.
The declared dimension must match the producing model — a hard error, and the first thing to check. Keyword: check the dimensions.
Exhaustive is exact and only viable at modest scale; approximate trades a little recall for a large speed gain. Keyword: recall vs latency.
Cosine is the usual choice for text embeddings. Keyword: cosine for text.
The mechanism for calling a model from T-SQL — which means the database now makes outbound calls that must be secured and monitored. Keyword: outbound from the DB.
Use a managed identity rather than a key, the same ranking applied everywhere else. Keyword: no stored key.
